directAnswer: Pope John XVIII, born John Fasanus, reigned from Christmas 1003 to 1009. Elected under the influence of the Crescentii, he approved the new diocese of Bamberg at the request of King Henry II and ended his life as a monk at St. Paul Outside the Walls.

paras: John Fasanus was a Roman cleric, a cardinal-priest of St. Peter's at the time of his election. He took office on 25 December 1003, through the influence of the patrician John Crescentius. Although the emperors claimed authority over Rome, the city in his time remained under local noble control.

His most significant act came at the request of King Henry II of Germany. Henry wanted to found a new diocese at Bamberg, and in 1007 John approved it, placing it under special papal protection. Henry went on to make Bamberg a center of church life in his kingdom. John also confirmed privileges for monasteries and kept up correspondence with bishops north of the Alps.

Toward the end of his life, John left the papal office and became a monk at the monastery of St. Paul Outside the Walls, where he died. Historians generally believe he abdicated in 1009, although the exact circumstances are uncertain. He was buried at St. Paul's.

keyFacts: Elected with the support of the patrician John Crescentius
Approved the diocese of Bamberg for Henry II (1007)
Retired as a monk at St. Paul Outside the Walls

faqs.question: Why is John XVIII linked with Bamberg?
faqs.answer: He approved the founding of the diocese of Bamberg in 1007 at the request of King Henry II, who later became emperor.

faqs.question: Did John XVIII resign?
faqs.answer: He appears to have left office and become a monk at St. Paul Outside the Walls, where he died, though the exact details are unclear.
